60	    if not path.exists():

1	# LunarWing XMPP Test Environment Setup
2	
3	This is the practical setup guide for the local LunarWing and XMPP bridge test
4	environment created by `scripts/lunarwing-xmpp-test-env.sh`.
5	
6	The test environment is isolated from your normal `~/.ironclaw` state. By
7	default it lives at:
8	
9	```bash
10	/tmp/lunarwing-xmpp-test
11	```
12	
13	Use this harness when you want to test:
14	
15	- the `xmpp-bridge` sidecar HTTP API
16	- bearer-token enforcement on the bridge
17	- live XMPP bridge configuration
18	- LunarWing running against isolated state
19	- user-systemd service behavior
20	
21	The `customic/` tree is not part of this setup.
22	
23	## 1. Pick a Test Root
24	
25	Use the default `/tmp` root for throwaway tests:
26	
27	```bash
28	cd /home/cmc/lunarwing/ic
29	scripts/lunarwing-xmpp-test-env.sh init
30	```
31	
32	Use a persistent root when you want the same env, logs, database, and OMEMO
33	store after reboot:
34	
35	```bash
36	cd /home/cmc/lunarwing/ic
37	export LUNARWING_TEST_ROOT="$HOME/.local/state/lunarwing-xmpp-test"
38	scripts/lunarwing-xmpp-test-env.sh init
39	```
40	
41	Keep that `LUNARWING_TEST_ROOT` exported for later commands in the same shell.
42	If you open a new shell, export it again before using the harness.
43	
44	## 2. Inspect the Generated Files
45	
46	After `init`, the harness creates:
47	
48	```text
49	$LUNARWING_TEST_ROOT/
50	  env/
51	    lunarwing.env
52	    xmpp-bridge.env
53	  logs/
54	  run/
55	  state/
56	    xmpp/
57	  systemd/
58	```
59	
60	If `LUNARWING_TEST_ROOT` is not set, replace it with
61	`/tmp/lunarwing-xmpp-test` in the paths above.
62	
63	The env files are mode `0600`. They may contain tokens and XMPP passwords.
64	Do not paste their contents into chat, issues, logs, or command output.
65	
66	Use the example files in this directory only as references:
67	
68	- `testing/lunarwing-xmpp/lunarwing.env.example`
69	- `testing/lunarwing-xmpp/xmpp-bridge.env.example`
70	
71	Edit the generated env files, not the examples.
72	
73	## 3. Build the Test Binaries
74	
75	Build both the current LunarWing binary and the bridge:
76	
77	```bash
78	scripts/lunarwing-xmpp-test-env.sh build
79	```
80	
81	This builds:
82	
83	```text
84	target/debug/ironclaw
85	bridges/xmpp-bridge/target/debug/xmpp-bridge
86	```
87	
88	The binary is still named `ironclaw` in the current codebase, even though the
89	project is now called LunarWing.
90	
91	For release binaries:
92	
93	```bash
94	export LUNARWING_TEST_PROFILE=release
95	scripts/lunarwing-xmpp-test-env.sh build
96	```
97	
98	Use the same `LUNARWING_TEST_PROFILE` for later `start-*`, `smoke`, and
99	`render-systemd` commands.
100	
101	## Service Names
102	
103	The harness intentionally renders test services by default:
104	
105	```text
106	lunarwing-test.service
107	xmpp-bridge-test.service
108	```
109	
110	Those names avoid clobbering a real user or system service named
111	`lunarwing.service`, `ironclaw.service`, or `xmpp-bridge.service`.
112	
113	When you want the generated units to use the real LunarWing name, set both
114	service-name variables before rendering:
115	
116	```bash
117	export LUNARWING_TEST_SERVICE_NAME=lunarwing.service
118	export LUNARWING_TEST_BRIDGE_SERVICE_NAME=xmpp-bridge.service
119	scripts/lunarwing-xmpp-test-env.sh render-systemd
120	```
121	
122	The harness uses the same names everywhere it generates dependencies:
123	
124	- the bridge unit gets `PartOf=$LUNARWING_TEST_SERVICE_NAME`
125	- the LunarWing unit gets `Wants=` and `After=` for
126	  `$LUNARWING_TEST_BRIDGE_SERVICE_NAME`
127	- `configure-bridge --restart` passes the bridge service name through
128	  `XMPP_BRIDGE_SERVICE`
129	
130	For generated user services, `configure-bridge --restart` uses
131	`systemctl --user` by default. For a machine-level service, set:
132	
133	```bash
134	export LUNARWING_TEST_SYSTEMCTL_SCOPE=system
135	```
136	
137	If you use the watchdog with a renamed service, point it at the same main unit:
138	
139	```bash
140	LUNARWING_WATCHDOG_SERVICE=lunarwing.service scripts/lunarwing-watchdog.sh
141	```
142	
143	## 4. Run the Local Bridge Smoke Test
144	
145	The bridge does not need live XMPP credentials for API smoke testing.
146	
147	```bash
148	scripts/lunarwing-xmpp-test-env.sh smoke
149	```
150	
151	That command:
152	
153	1. starts `xmpp-bridge` if it is not already running
154	2. calls `/v1/status` without a bearer token and expects rejection
155	3. calls `/v1/status` with the generated token and expects success
156	4. prints bridge status
157	5. stops the bridge unless `LUNARWING_TEST_KEEP_BRIDGE=1` is set
158	
159	To keep the bridge running after the smoke test:
160	
161	```bash
162	LUNARWING_TEST_KEEP_BRIDGE=1 scripts/lunarwing-xmpp-test-env.sh smoke
163	```
164	
165	Manual bridge commands:
166	
167	```bash
168	scripts/lunarwing-xmpp-test-env.sh start-bridge
169	scripts/lunarwing-xmpp-test-env.sh bridge-auth-check
170	scripts/lunarwing-xmpp-test-env.sh bridge-status
171	scripts/lunarwing-xmpp-test-env.sh stop-bridge
172	```
173	
174	## 5. Configure Live XMPP
175	
176	Only do this after the local bridge smoke test passes.
177	
178	Open the generated bridge env file:
179	
180	```bash
181	${EDITOR:-nano} "${LUNARWING_TEST_ROOT:-/tmp/lunarwing-xmpp-test}/env/xmpp-bridge.env"
182	```
183	
184	Set:
185	
186	```bash
187	XMPP_JID=your-account@example.org
188	XMPP_PASSWORD=your-xmpp-password
189	XMPP_ALLOW_ROOMS_JSON=["room@conference.example.org"]
190	```
191	
192	Optional but useful:
193	
194	```bash
195	XMPP_ALLOW_FROM_JSON=["trusted-user@example.org"]
196	XMPP_DM_POLICY=allowlist
197	XMPP_ENCRYPTED_ROOMS_JSON=[]
198	XMPP_RESOURCE=lunarwing-test
199	```
200	
201	Start the bridge and apply the live config:
202	
203	```bash
204	scripts/lunarwing-xmpp-test-env.sh start-bridge
205	scripts/lunarwing-xmpp-test-env.sh configure-bridge --show-status room@conference.example.org
206	```
207	
208	If you use `XMPP_ALLOW_ROOMS_JSON` instead of command-line room args:
209	
210	```bash
211	scripts/lunarwing-xmpp-test-env.sh configure-bridge --show-status
212	```
213	
214	Check status:
215	
216	```bash
217	scripts/lunarwing-xmpp-test-env.sh bridge-status
218	```
219	
220	## 6. Set a Safe Outbound Rate Limit
221	
222	Before sending live test traffic, set a conservative outbound cap:
223	
224	```bash
225	scripts/lunarwing-xmpp-test-env.sh rate-limit status
226	scripts/lunarwing-xmpp-test-env.sh rate-limit set 20 --reset
227	```
228	
229	To pause outbound sends:
230	
231	```bash
232	scripts/lunarwing-xmpp-test-env.sh rate-limit off --reset
233	```
234	
235	To clear the rolling counter while keeping the current cap:
236	
237	```bash
238	scripts/lunarwing-xmpp-test-env.sh rate-limit reset
239	```
240	
241	The live override resets when `xmpp-bridge` restarts.
242	
243	## 7. Run LunarWing Against the Test State
244	
245	If you only need bridge testing, skip this section.
246	
247	The harness starts LunarWing with the isolated `IRONCLAW_BASE_DIR` from
248	`env/lunarwing.env`:
249	
250	```bash
251	scripts/lunarwing-xmpp-test-env.sh start-lunarwing
252	scripts/lunarwing-xmpp-test-env.sh lunarwing-status
253	```
254	
255	Stop it with:
256	
257	```bash
258	scripts/lunarwing-xmpp-test-env.sh stop-lunarwing
259	```
260	
261	Default command:
262	
263	```bash
264	target/debug/ironclaw --no-onboard run
265	```
266	
267	If LunarWing needs onboarding or provider credentials, run onboarding against
268	the isolated env:
269	
270	```bash
271	set -a
272	. "${LUNARWING_TEST_ROOT:-/tmp/lunarwing-xmpp-test}/env/lunarwing.env"
273	set +a
274	target/debug/ironclaw onboard
275	```
276	
277	Then start LunarWing again through the harness.
278	
279	To pass a custom command line:
280	
281	```bash
282	scripts/lunarwing-xmpp-test-env.sh start-lunarwing -- --no-onboard --no-db run
283	```
284	
285	## 8. Generate User-Systemd Units
286	
287	Generate test units using the current checkout, test root, and profile:
288	
289	```bash
290	scripts/lunarwing-xmpp-test-env.sh render-systemd
291	```
292	
293	Install them for your user:
294	
295	```bash
296	mkdir -p ~/.config/systemd/user
297	cp "${LUNARWING_TEST_ROOT:-/tmp/lunarwing-xmpp-test}/systemd/"*.service ~/.config/systemd/user/
298	systemctl --user daemon-reload
299	```
300	
301	Start the bridge service first:
302	
303	```bash
304	systemctl --user start xmpp-bridge-test.service
305	systemctl --user status xmpp-bridge-test.service
306	```
307	
308	Then start LunarWing:
309	
310	```bash
311	systemctl --user start lunarwing-test.service
312	systemctl --user status lunarwing-test.service
313	```
314	
315	Use read-only diagnostics first:
316	
317	```bash
318	systemctl --user show xmpp-bridge-test.service
319	journalctl --user -u xmpp-bridge-test.service -n 100 --no-pager
320	scripts/lunarwing-xmpp-test-env.sh bridge-status
321	```
322	
323	Stop services:
324	
325	```bash
326	systemctl --user stop lunarwing-test.service
327	systemctl --user stop xmpp-bridge-test.service
328	```
329	
330	The bridge unit has `PartOf=lunarwing-test.service`, so LunarWing service stops
331	can also stop the bridge.
332	
333	The built-in Rust service installer is separate from this test renderer. Running
334	`ironclaw service install` now installs the user unit as `lunarwing.service` and
335	attempts to disable the legacy `ironclaw.service` user unit when it exists.
336	
337	For production system services, use the committed templates instead of the
338	generated user-service units:
339	
340	```bash
341	sudo install -o root -g root -m 0644 systemd/xmpp-bridge.service /etc/systemd/system/xmpp-bridge.service
342	sudo install -o root -g root -m 0644 systemd/lunarwing.service /etc/systemd/system/lunarwing.service
343	sudo systemctl daemon-reload
344	sudo systemctl enable --now xmpp-bridge.service
345	sudo systemctl enable --now lunarwing.service
346	```
347	
348	Those templates expect `/etc/lunarwing/lunarwing.env` and
349	`/etc/lunarwing/xmpp-bridge.env` for production config and secrets.
350	
351	Install the production watchdog timer with:
352	
353	```bash
354	sudo scripts/install-lunarwing-watchdog.sh
355	sudo systemctl status lunarwing-watchdog.timer --no-pager
356	```
357	
358	Migration note: the installer disables/removes old `ironclaw-watchdog` units and
359	the old `/usr/local/sbin/ironclaw-watchdog` binary before installing the renamed
360	watchdog.
361	
362	## 9. Troubleshoot
363	
364	Run:
365	
366	```bash
367	scripts/lunarwing-xmpp-test-env.sh doctor
368	scripts/lunarwing-xmpp-test-env.sh logs 120
369	```
370	
371	Common issues:
372	
373	- `HTTP 000` from `doctor` means nothing is listening on the bridge port.
374	- `401` or `403` from `bridge-status` usually means the wrong token or env file.
375	- A system bridge may already be using `127.0.0.1:8787`; change
376	  `XMPP_BRIDGE_BIND` in the generated bridge env file.
377	- `configure-bridge` requires `jq`, `curl`, `XMPP_BRIDGE_TOKEN`, and
378	  `XMPP_PASSWORD`.
379	- If the generated systemd unit points at a missing binary, rerun `build` with
380	  the same `LUNARWING_TEST_PROFILE` used for `render-systemd`.
381	
382	## 10. Clean Up
383	
384	Stop harness-managed processes:
385	
386	```bash
387	scripts/lunarwing-xmpp-test-env.sh stop-lunarwing
388	scripts/lunarwing-xmpp-test-env.sh stop-bridge
389	```
390	
391	Stop user services if you installed them:
392	
393	```bash
394	systemctl --user stop lunarwing-test.service
395	systemctl --user stop xmpp-bridge-test.service
396	```
397	
398	Remove generated throwaway state only when you are sure you do not need the
399	logs, database, or OMEMO store:
400	
401	```bash
402	rm -rf "${LUNARWING_TEST_ROOT:-/tmp/lunarwing-xmpp-test}"
403	```

9	#   - Cloud SQL Auth Proxy accessible via IAM

13	
14	# Must run as root
15	if [ "$(id -u)" -ne 0 ]; then
16	  echo "ERROR: This script must be run as root (sudo bash setup.sh)"
17	  exit 1

21	apt-get update
22	apt-get install -y docker.io
23	systemctl enable docker
24	systemctl start docker
25

27	CLOUD_SQL_PROXY_VERSION="v2.14.3"
28	CLOUD_SQL_PROXY_SHA256="75e7cc1f158ab6f97b7810e9d8419c55735cff40bc56d4f19673adfdf2406a59"
29	curl -fsSL -o /usr/local/bin/cloud-sql-proxy \
30	  "https://storage.googleapis.com/cloud-sql-connectors/cloud-sql-proxy/${CLOUD_SQL_PROXY_VERSION}/cloud-sql-proxy.linux.amd64"
31	echo "${CLOUD_SQL_PROXY_SHA256}  /usr/local/bin/cloud-sql-proxy" | sha256sum -c - || {
32	  echo "ERROR: Cloud SQL Auth Proxy checksum verification failed -- aborting"
33	  rm -f /usr/local/bin/cloud-sql-proxy

36	chmod +x /usr/local/bin/cloud-sql-proxy

46

52	# Owned by root, readable only by root. Docker reads --env-file as root

71	echo ""
72	echo "Verify with:"

74	echo "  systemctl status ironclaw"
75	echo "  docker logs ironclaw"
